The People's Protector

By: Siniketiwe Hlanze | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We unpack the Public Protector's adverse findings against The President and what it means for his future

Unique Selling Point:
Public Protector Busisiwe Mkhwebane's recent reports have been the subject matter of a political furore. Insert will unpack these and highlight some of her contentious findings and the political consequences
of the political figures implicated.

Summary:
In the last two months, advocate Busisiwe Mkhwebane has released reports that have been met with great push back. In her recent report she has found that President Ramaphosa misled parliament in his explanation of funds which were deposited into his campaign account. She has also concluded that there's merit to money laundering suspicions due to how this money was transfered into the account. Although she was a firm favourite during the interview process, with only the Democratic Alliance raising concern over her ability to take over the Public Protector's office. She has come under intense scrutiny following some of her findings in various reports. She's erred in judgment in three major cases, The Vrede Dairy Farm Project, ABSA and SARS. In the two most recent reports Mkhwebane has been accused of spurring factional battles within the ruling party and her credibility to lead the prestigious office has been questioned.

The insert will unpack the following:
Political implications of Mkhwebane's report on Ramaphosa
The ANC's response to Mkhwebane's report - as well as what this means for party funding
Political implications of Mkhwebane's report on Pravin Gordhan
The ramifications of The Public Protector's office credibility if reports are constantly taken on review


Further information:
Who Are the Untouchable:
There seems to be great hysteria when certain political figures are being brought to book. Minister Pravin Gordhan and President Cyril Ramaphosa are perceived to be beacons of clean governance however when they are investigated as in this instance, it is viewed as an attack and no longer an exercise in the interest of governance and transparency.

An interview with Busisiwe Mkhwebane (or office rep) will speak about how her office has come under attack following her recent reports.What she makes of judgments made against her and how these reflect on her ability lead her office.

Political Analyst Mcebisi Ndletyana will give analysis on how Mkhwebane's reports have influenced politics as well as the reaction by President Ramaphosa and Min Pravin Gordhan.

Professor Bernard Bekink will reflect on how Mkhwebane has fared in office thus far and questions around her credibility and understanding of the law

James Motlatsi, long time friend to Ramaphosa and CR17 campaign manager, will speak about how there was nothing untoward about the donations made to the campaign.

Pravin Gordhan will reflect on findings made against him in SARS Rogue Unit and Ivan Pillay reports by Public Protector

The ANC (spokesperson or SG Ace Magashule) will reflect on whether or not they are concerned that their leader has been found to have lied to parliament and problematic trend of party funding

Ace Magashule ANC SG

Press Release:


The People’s Protector
Before taking the Public Protector Busisiwe Mkhwebane’s adverse report against him on urgent judicial review, President Cyril Ramaphosa lambasted it, calling it “fundamentally and irretrievably flawed”. Then the Constitutional Court upheld a scathing High Court judgment against her – admonishing the Public Protector for dishonesty and acting in bad faith. With her battle against Minister Pravin Gordhan still playing out in court, in recent days, Mkhwebane has taken a very public lashing. Now her credibility and integrity are at stake, but can she claw her way back from the edge?
Producer: Siniketiwe Hlanze
Presenter: Derek Watts

And it would be a bit unfair to say because there has been a few cases that have been reviewed and I supposed what is interesting at the moment and what is on everybody’s liips is the recent judgment by the constitutional court to say say you know definitely she hasn’t fulfilled any of her duties but the duties of the public protector are vast and if we are going to decide wheather she has done a good job we need to look at it wholistically.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We unpack the Public Protector's adverse findings against The President and what it means for his future
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Public Protector Busisiwe Mkhwebane's recent reports have been the subject matter of a political furore. Insert will unpack these and highlight some of her contentious findings and the political consequences of the political figures implicated.
metadata.Summary: In the last two months, advocate Busisiwe Mkhwebane has released reports that have been met with great push back. In her recent report she has found that President Ramaphosa misled parliament in his explanation of funds which were deposited into his campaign account. She has also concluded that there's merit to money laundering suspicions due to how this money was transfered into the account. Although she was a firm favourite during the interview process, with only the Democratic Alliance raising concern over her ability to take over the Public Protector's office. She has come under intense scrutiny following some of her findings in various reports. She's erred in judgment in three major cases, The Vrede Dairy Farm Project, ABSA and SARS. In the two most recent reports Mkhwebane has been accused of spurring factional battles within the ruling party and her credibility to lead the prestigious office has been questioned. The insert will unpack the following: Political implications of Mkhwebane's report on Ramaphosa The ANC's response to Mkhwebane's report - as well as what this means for party funding Political implications of Mkhwebane's report on Pravin Gordhan The ramifications of The Public Protector's office credibility if reports are constantly taken on review
metadata.Further information: Who Are the Untouchable: There seems to be great hysteria when certain political figures are being brought to book. Minister Pravin Gordhan and President Cyril Ramaphosa are perceived to be beacons of clean governance however when they are investigated as in this instance, it is viewed as an attack and no longer an exercise in the interest of governance and transparency. An interview with Busisiwe Mkhwebane (or office rep) will speak about how her office has come under attack following her recent reports.What she makes of judgments made against her and how these reflect on her ability lead her office. Political Analyst Mcebisi Ndletyana will give analysis on how Mkhwebane's reports have influenced politics as well as the reaction by President Ramaphosa and Min Pravin Gordhan. Professor Bernard Bekink will reflect on how Mkhwebane has fared in office thus far and questions around her credibility and understanding of the law James Motlatsi, long time friend to Ramaphosa and CR17 campaign manager, will speak about how there was nothing untoward about the donations made to the campaign. Pravin Gordhan will reflect on findings made against him in SARS Rogue Unit and Ivan Pillay reports by Public Protector The ANC (spokesperson or SG Ace Magashule) will reflect on whether or not they are concerned that their leader has been found to have lied to parliament and problematic trend of party funding
